subjects.displayTitle: Love at the foundation: creation, religion, and human fellowship
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh places love at both ends of religion: it begins as love for God and for His Chosen Ones, and it is fulfilled only when that love reaches His servants. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá turns it toward the stranger, asking us to cleanse our eyes until no one looks foreign, and he warns that a religion which breeds hatred has lost its reason for being. This love is more than a moral counsel. It is the motive of creation itself, the attraction that binds the elements and moves the spheres, the clay from which the human heart was molded and the paradise it is invited to enter. The First Epistle of John, with its account of the Son sent so that God’s love might be made known, offers a kindred movement from love received to love owed [1]. To take this seriously is to ask what in religion stays constant beneath its changing laws, to see love and unity as one reality from two sides, and to follow the pathways by which love travels from the Creator into friendship, hospitality and daily faithfulness.
subjects.arc: Begin with love’s expression in service, examine its implications for religious life, explore creation and spiritual attraction, and return through friendship and daily practice to wider voices.

order.why: Consider the reported criterion that religion should produce love rather than hatred.
shortened: The love of God haloes all created things. Were it not for the love of God, no animate being would exist.

Third, religion must be the mainspring and source of love in the world, for religion is the revelation of the will of God, the divine fundamental of which is love. Therefore, if religion should prove to be the cause of enmity and hatred instead of love, its absence is preferable to its existence.

order.why: Open with the movement from loving God to manifesting love to His servants.
shortened: The beginning of religion is love for God and for His Chosen Ones, and its end is to manifest that love to His servants.

order.why: Make companionship with friend and stranger the immediate consequence.
Read the challenge to the gaze that turns other people into strangers.
shortened: O ye lovers of this wronged one! Cleanse ye your eyes, so that ye behold no man as different from yourselves. See ye no strangers; rather see all men as friends, for love and unity come hard when ye fix your gaze on otherness. And in this new and wondrous age, the Holy Writings say that we must be at one with every people; that we must see neither harshness nor injustice, neither malevolence, nor hostility, nor hate, but rather turn our eyes toward the heaven of ancient glory.

order.why: Read love, unity, and harmony as necessary for fruitful deeds.
shortened: O maid-servant of God! Know thou, the first bounty from the True One is love, unity and harmony, and without these all the deeds pass in vain and give no result.

order.why: Keep the application of teachings in deeds at the center of friendship.
shortened: The revelation of the Eternal mystery y and its great wisdom and the grace of the Most Great Name and its blessed fruit require that the loved ones should be distinguished among all others in this new Cycle by their fellowship, their unity and their attraction and should be characterised in particular by their application in deeds of the instructions of that Ancient Beloved in this glorious Dispensation. Those instructions are none other than the strengthening of the sincere bonds of friendship amongst all God's creatures.

order.why: Read the reported connection between service to humanity and service to God.
shortened: Therefore, order your lives in accordance with the first principle of the divine teaching, which is love. Service to humanity is service to God. Let the love and light of the Kingdom radiate through you until all who look upon you shall be illumined by its reflection.

order.why: Consider sincerity and kindness as concrete expressions of heavenly love.
shortened: The beloved of God must be the cause of spreading the Heavenly Love. They must impart spiritual concord; deal with all men in the utmost sincerity and kindness in accord with the commands and exhortations of the Merciful One.

order.why: Read the reported distinction between outward professions and love born in hearts.
shortened: There are today many people in the world who hate each other heartily but outwardly they express love and friendship. We must do something so that real love may be born in the hearts and strangeness be removed.

order.why: Keep the reported removal of racial barriers joined to heartfelt action.
shortened: He broke all the imaginary luminations between the races. He took away these fetters and chains. We love the people with heart and soul and not only by mere word of mouth.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast between compulsion and willing response to love.
Read the reported declaration of love as the only weapon.
shortened: We have many enemies, bitter, dangerous and vengeful! But we defeat them through the Power of love! That is our only weapon.

order.why: Keep the minister’s reported conversation centered on charity, tolerance, and sympathy.
shortened: Let us have love and more love, a love that melts all opposition, a love that conquers all foes, a love that sweeps away all barriers, a love that aboundeth in charity, large-heartedness, tolerance, and noble-striving, a love that triumphs over all obstacles, a boundless, resistless, sweeping love.
Hast thou love? Then thy power is irresistible. Hast thou sympathy? Then all the stars will sing thy praise!

order.why: Read the reported Ridvan message extending love to strangers and the broken-hearted.
shortened: The message of Rizwan is love, love and still more love, love amongst the believers, love for the strangers, love for the fallen and broken-hearted, love for mankind. If thou hast a universe of love, hunger for more. Live in the world of love, swim in the ocean of love, soar in the atmosphere of love, walk in the bright realm of love, speak the words of love, practice the deeds of love, adore the Beloved of love, sing the soothing lullaby of love and advance toward the palace of love.

order.why: Consider all-embracing love as the essence of the teaching.
Read friendship as the purpose of revelation and sacred books.
shortened: The advent of the prophets and the revelation of the Holy Books is intended to create love between souls and friendship between the inhabitants of the earth. Real love is impossible unless one turn his face towards God and be attracted to His Beauty.

order.why: Keep the reported connection between that purpose and endured hardship.
shortened: The aim of the appearance of all the Manifestations of God, the prophets and the revelation of all the holy books has been to create Love between the hearts. His Holiness Baha'u'llah accepted so much hardships so that love may be created in the hearts.

order.why: Read the parallel concise report about prophetic purpose.
shortened: The aim of the appearance of all the Prophets - the Manifestations of the holy, divine verities, the revelations of the holy Scriptures has been for the creation of love in the hearts of men.

order.why: Consider the law of love amid changing ordinances.
Read love and kindliness without limitations as the foundation of faith.
shortened: In this divine cycle and merciful manifestation, the very foundation of God's Faith is love and kindliness, though not bound by any limitations.

order.why: Keep the call to amity and peace addressed to all nations.
shortened: The Faith of the Blessed Beauty is summoning mankind to safety and love, to amity and peace; it hath raised up its tabernacle on the heights of the earth, and directeth its call to all nations.

order.why: Read the account of sacrifice directed toward ending strife and planting faithfulness.
Bring love and unity into the needs of the body politic.
shortened: Love and unity are the needs of the body politic today. Without these there can be no progress or prosperity attained. Therefore, the friends of God must adhere to the power which will create this love and unity in the hearts of the sons of men.

order.why: Read peace, affinity, and love as the quickening spirit of the age.
shortened: Verily the Spirit through which the temple of the contingent world shall be quickened in this time is indeed the founder of peace, the spirit of affinity and the light of love.

order.why: Keep divine love, peace, and the welfare of nations together.
shortened: Today, the world-illumining light is the radiance of divine love and the effulgence of the Most Great Peace and the welfare of nations.

order.why: Read the reported account of order through justice, culture, and philanthropy.
Consider the reported intention to establish harmony among people.
Read unity as the expression of loving power.
shortened: Unity is the expression of the loving power of God and reflects the reality of Divinity.

order.why: Keep the reported inseparability of unity and love.
shortened: Unity is love. It cannot be established without love. Therefore try, as far as possible, to be filled with love. Love is perpetual life, the most perfect vitality.

order.why: Read the reported hope of a new foundation and complete harmony.
shortened: I desire to make manifest among the friends in America a new light that they may become a new people, that a new foundation may be established and complete harmony be realized; for the foundation of Baha'u'llah is love.

order.why: Consider the reported tree and shower of mercy as images of shared nurture.
Read love as the reported first sign of faith and a light to diffuse.
shortened: The first sign of faith is love. The message of the holy, divine Manifestations is love; the phenomena of creation are based upon love; the radiance of the world is due to love; the well-being and happiness of the world depend upon it. Therefore, I admonish you that you must strive throughout the human world to diffuse the light of love.

order.why: Follow the reported burning of veils toward virtue, healing, and consolation.
shortened: By the fire of the Love of God the veil is burnt which separates us from the Heavenly Realities, and with clear vision we are enabled to struggle onward and upward, ever progressing in the paths of virtue and holiness, and becoming the means of light to the world.

There is nothing greater or more blessed than the Love of God! It gives healing to the sick, balm to the wounded, joy and consolation to the whole world, and through it alone can man attain Life Everlasting. The essence of all religions is the Love of God, and it is the foundation of all the sacred teachings.

order.why: Keep the reported counsel to show love to all.
Read the Hidden Words’ images of creation, nearness, dignity, and divine love within.
shortened: I loved thy creation, hence I created thee. Wherefore, do thou love Me, that I may name thy name and fill thy soul with the spirit of life.
My love is in thee, know it, that thou mayest find Me near unto thee.

Noble I made thee, wherewith dost thou abase thyself? Out of the essence of knowledge I gave thee being, why seekest thou enlightenment from anyone beside Me? Out of the clay of love I molded thee, how dost thou busy thyself with another? Turn thy sight unto thyself, that thou mayest find Me standing within thee, mighty, powerful and self-subsisting.

order.why: Connect creation through love with fellowship and unity.
Read the cited Hidden Treasure tradition as the source’s explanation of creation.
shortened: The cause of the creation of all contingent beings has been love, as is referred to in the well-known tradition which says: "I was a Hidden Treasure and I loved to be known, and therefore I created the creation that I might be known."

order.why: Keep that tradition alongside love as the light of creation.
Consider the commentary’s different stations and magnetism of oneness.
shortened: For the variation in the stations of love are from differences of stations and stages and in each world of the worlds and in each stage of the stages there can be seen a magnetism of oneness .  Within the grasp of its power is the mutual attraction of the reality of all things and the pulling [together] of the subtlety of Being.  And this magnetism of oneness is the station of Love and Attraction (khullat ).

order.why: Read the Tablet of Love’s extended account of life, connection, and civilization.
shortened: Know thou of a certainty that Love is the secret of God's holy Dispensation, the manifestation of the All-Merciful, the fountain of spiritual outpourings. Love is heaven's kindly light, the Holy Spirit's eternal breath that vivifieth the human soul. Love is the cause of God's revelation unto man, the vital bond inherent, in accordance with the divine creation, in the realities of things.
Love is the spirit of life unto the adorned body of mankind, the establisher of true civilization in this mortal world, and the shedder of imperishable glory upon every high-aiming race and nation.

order.why: Keep the reported claim about love and the origin of creation attributed.
Read the concise praise of love adorning the world.
Consider wine before the vine as poetic language about creation’s cause.
Read the paradox of love as both affliction and its remedy.
Keep the source’s acknowledgment that many volumes cannot exhaust love’s mystery.
shortened: How wondrous is this most great mystery of love! Though a thousand volumes be written about it, it would still appear deficient. It is the first adornment and the cause and reason for the continuation of existence. In one station it bestows life and grants spirit, in another it makes one utterly evanescent, and in yet another it confers an enduring, eternal power.

order.why: Distinguish the incomprehensible divine Reality from its manifestation as love.
Defines love for humanity as the common foundation of religion.
Consider the answering relation of divine love and human love.
Read the reported four kinds of love in their theological setting.
shortened: In the Gospel it is said God is love.

There are four kinds of love. The first is the love that flows from God to man; it consists of the inexhaustible graces, the Divine effulgence and heavenly illumination. Through this love the world of being receives life. Through this love man is endowed with physical existence, until, through the breath of the Holy Spirit -- this same love -- he receives eternal life and becomes the image of the Living God. This love is the origin of all the love in the world of creation.

order.why: Follow the mirror image from divine radiance to love between people.
Keep the reported one sun reflected in many hearts.
shortened: Such is the true Baha'i love.
Your hearts must be like mirrors brightly polished, which reflect the light of the One sun. This love never changes no matter what its form, because it is from the One Sun - the One Love.

order.why: Read universal attraction as the source’s account of physical and spiritual connection.
shortened: O thou who art yearning to discover! The discoverers of the mysteries of existence and those who comprehend the qualities and hidden secrets hold that a wondrous force of attraction and a strange magnetic power of connection permeates and encompasses all these infinite beings and successive contingent things, both physical and spiritual, and is equally present in them all.

In truth, every thing has unveiled itself through that universal attractive force with a manifestation and light and has displayed its beauty. And in human reality it has become the power of yearning, bringing about enthusiasm and passion and attraction.

order.why: Consider love as the moving principle within this theological explanation.
Keep gravitation, affinity, and electric energy in the source’s analogical language.
Read the reported relation between attraction and continued existence.
shortened: All union of hearts in this world is brought about by the power of attraction or love. The life of the whole world depends upon it, and when this power of attraction or love is gone, then all is disunion and annihilation then takes place.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast of love with the forces of disintegration.
Read the body, fruitless tree, and unlit lamp as images of connection.
Keep the reported dependence of spiritual life and illumination on love.
Read the reported Christian appeal to God as love.
Consider love’s outpouring in relation to human impulses.
shortened: Although in the world of existence the Outpourings of the Almighty are infinite yet the Greatest Divine Outpouring is the "Love of God." This is the dominant, transcendental Power which rises above all the natural susceptibilities of the world of humanity.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of a center from which love radiates.
Read the affirmation of love as the fundamental basis.
Consider the concise statement of love’s incomparable bounty.
shortened: There is no grace greater in the world of existence than this love. It is the most mighty sign the most wondrous bounty to the world of humanity.

order.why: Read the brief identification of love with the religion of the righteous.
Keep the reported nut and shell image as a distinction of essence and form.
shortened: The essence of all essences is love, which is likened unto the meat of the nut, while all else is likened unto the shell or outside. Through the providence of the Blessed Perfection our spirits must be full of the love of God.

order.why: Read the reported description of love as spiritual life.
shortened: Tell them that Love is the one great thing. - It is life - the only life of the spirit.

order.why: Consider love as nourishment at the reported divine table.
shortened: Some of the heavenly tables are the divine teachings and their power and effect will be everlasting. Another of the godly tables is His love, which is the cause of Eternal Life.

order.why: Read the reported movement from creation toward reflecting love.
shortened: Through the manifestation of Love God created Man. To attain a supreme station man must reflect the Love of God.

order.why: Consider the reported relation of love to virtues and progress.
Keep the reported distinction of humanity through love and happiness.
Read the reported claim about the endurance of a spiritual bond.
Consider the reported love that overcomes barriers.
shortened: There is only one love which is infinite and unlimited and divine, and that is the love which comes with the Breath of the Holy Spirit - the Love of God - which breaks all barriers and sweeps all before it.

order.why: Keep the concise reported magnet image.
shortened: In the world of existence there is no more powerful magnet than the magnet of love.

order.why: Read love as traversing distance and imagination in a single step.
shortened: This matter is a matter of love - what a wonderful rider it is and what a wonderful walker! It traverses the globe in a single step and crosses the realm of imagination in an instant.

order.why: Consider a gesture communicating the illumination of a longing heart.
Read the reported bodily effects of spiritual emotion.
shortened: Real Love is a spiritual thing. It is an emotion of the soul. From the emotion of the soul an effect is also produced upon the body. Love will cause the heart to burn and the eyes to weep - it will shake the body and render sleepless the mind.

order.why: Keep the reported turning toward God and separation from other desires.
shortened: If your hearts are turned always towards God, and filled with the love of God, that love will separate them from all other things, that love will be the wall that will come between them and every other desire.

order.why: Consider divine friendship and the burning away of estrangement.
Read attraction as willing and joyful service.
Keep the call to give love an embodied expression.
Consider the reported lamp’s need for prepared means as a challenge to put love into practice.
Read the reported home as a place for learning love.
shortened: This is the home of Love, those who come in must learn the lessons of love, thus they may know how to love each other.

order.why: Keep hospitality, truthfulness, humility, and reverence alongside affection.
shortened: The abundancies of God are, to love each other, to speak the truth, to cut our hearts from the world, to be reverent, to be humble, to be hospitable.

order.why: Consider the reported preparation and sharing of food in love.
shortened: A food that is prepared in love and partaken of in love gives one great delight. Nay, whatever is done with love imparts great delight.

order.why: Read the reported willingness to make time for what is done in love.
Keep the strong reported condiment image in its own figurative voice.
Read the related reported transformation of bitterness.
Consider the reported faithfulness that preserves love over time.
shortened: In the world of existence nothing is greater than faithfulness, for it allows love to remain unimpaired in spite of the length of time.

order.why: Keep the source’s description of an old friendship rooted in spirit.
Read friends and companions as pearls in love’s ocean.
Consider the reported friendship sustained for God’s sake.
Keep the reported distinction of direct and indirect love.
Read the reported image of each person as a letter from the Beloved.
Consider the reported movement from overcoming estrangement to willing attention.
shortened: One must love so that souls become beloved and their estrangement disappears. You must love so that they will love you. When they love you, they will listen to your words. The foundation of God's Cause and the purpose of religion is love.

order.why: Read people as branches growing from the same tree of love.
shortened: And the Love of God will attract pure hearts so that they should love one another as Branches grown from the Tree of the Love of God, as His believers who have attached themselves to His Word, baptized with the Holy Spirit which is pouring today from the Kingdom of Holinesses.

order.why: Keep the reported connection between mutual love and confirmation.
Read the reported counsel to hold to what produces friendship.
Retain the personal report of joyful attraction and praise.
shortened: Jinab-i-Amin is present and offers utmost praise for all the friends and handmaidens of the Merciful, that all are intoxicated with the wine of divine love and are drunkards in the wine-house of the love of God, taking in hand the cup of the wine of the knowledge of God and dancing and stamping their feet, raising from heart and soul the cry of "O Glory of the Most Glorious!"

order.why: Consider the reported daily pattern of love, work, prayer, peace, and joy.
Read the reported image of love as the human tree’s fruit.
shortened: Man is like a tree. The tree lives to produce fruit. The fruit of man is love.

order.why: Keep the related supplied report and its original wording.
shortened: The true fruit of man is therefore Love. The purpose of a tee is to produce fruit. Man is like a tree. His fruit should be Love.

order.why: Consider warmth and illumination beyond the accumulation of books.
Close the linked readings with a heart at rest in love for all peoples.
Read the supplied provisional rendering of universal attraction without merging translations.
shortened: Those who discover the secrets of the universe, and are aware of its inherent properties and concealed mysteries believe that an astonishing power of attraction is diffused throughout creation; that an extraordinary bond of magnetism embraceth these myriad beings and governeth these countless elements, both physical and spiritual.

That universal power of attraction is manifest within the inmost reality of every being with an ever-varying splendour, its beauty and charm made apparent in different degrees. Within the inmost reality of man, it expresseth itself as the power of yearning, which is conducive to rapture, fervour, and ecstasy.

order.why: Preserve the supplied Hidden Treasure passage and its extended attribution for comparison.
Read the two supplied renderings of the law of love as distinct textual witnesses.
Keep the supplied Paris Talks statement about the prophets’ message.
Read the supplied letter symbolism of love in its provisional translation.
shortened: God grant that thou mayest fix thy gaze upon the love of God which is the generating impulse and the purpose underlying the whole of creation, and mayest be set aglow by its heat. Through its first letter, (Ha'), the fire of His love gloweth in the hearts of the favoured among the faithful, and in the breasts of they who are nigh unto God and are devoted to Him. Through its second, (Ba'), all created things are made manifest and, by the very dot beneath it, hath appeared the realm of distinction.

order.why: Consider the supplied Atharva Veda invocation within its own devotional tradition.
Retain the saying attributed through Sophy Burnham without enlarging its provenance.
Close with the supplied Pope Francis statement on creation and love.

questions: What is involved in moving from love for God to love expressed toward people, especially strangers?
How might the effects of a religious practice reveal whether it is serving the purpose described in these readings?
What do the cosmic images of attraction and radiance contribute to the practical counsels about friendship and service?
How does 1 John connect receiving divine love with loving others, and what remains distinctive in its account of the Son?
What means would need to be prepared for love to become more than a profession of goodwill in a community?
How could daily habits of hospitality, faithfulness, and attention give a lasting form to love?

references.label: 1 · 1 John 4:7–12 · Divine love and mutual love
references.note: Read the King James Version’s movement from love originating in God to the responsibility to love one another. Compare it with the compilation’s movement from creation and revelation toward human fellowship, while retaining the epistle’s particular account of the sending of the Son.

subjects.displayTitle: Wealth and poverty: what we possess and what we become
subjects.introduction: Neither poverty nor wealth, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is praiseworthy or blameworthy in itself; each shows its worth only in what it makes of a person. Wealth earned by one’s own effort in commerce, agriculture, art or industry and spent for the good of others is praised in the highest degree, while the poor are called God’s trust among the rich, to be guarded from desperation, and begging in religion’s name is named the most abhorrent of deeds. Bahá’u’lláh does not soften the other side: riches are a mighty barrier between lover and beloved, few of the rich reach the city of contentment, and yet the one whose wealth does not hinder him shines on the dwellers of heaven like the sun. Underneath lies a different kind of riches, love, contentment, qualities no thief can carry off. Agur’s prayer in Proverbs, asking for neither poverty nor riches but enough, names the twin temptations exactly [1]. From here the road leads into conduct in business, the moderation of inequality, frugality and simplicity, and the prayer for prosperity.
subjects.arc: Begin by judging wealth through its fruits, establish honest livelihood and care for the poor, examine attachment and instability, then explore contentment and enduring spiritual riches.

order.why: Consider both wealth’s danger and the possibility of a rich person illuminating others.
shortened: Know ye in truth that wealth is a mighty barrier between the seeker and his desire, the lover and his beloved. The rich, but for a few, shall in no wise attain the court of His presence nor enter the city of content and resignation. Well is it then with him, who, being rich, is not hindered by his riches from the eternal kingdom, nor deprived by them of imperishable dominion. By the Most Great Name! The splendor of such a wealthy man shall illuminate the dwellers of heaven even as the sun enlightens the people of the earth!

order.why: Open with the explicit refusal to judge wealth or poverty apart from their results.
shortened: Neither poverty nor wealth are, in reality, praiseworthy or blameworthy until the results of each are seen in each person. Often poverty becomes the cause of true wealth and vice versa, and often wealth becomes the cause of attaining God's good-pleasure and vice versa.

order.why: Read the praise of wealth honestly acquired and expended for philanthropic purposes.
Keep lawful enjoyment of material bounties alongside freedom from obstruction.
shortened: He whom nothing preventeth from God - no harm shall come to him though he adorn himself with the ornaments of the earth and its decorations and whatsoever hath been created therein, for God hath created all that is in the heavens and on earth for His servants who believe in His unity. Eat, O people, of that which God hath made lawful unto you and deprive not yourselves of His wondrous bounties.

order.why: Make protection from poverty and desperation an immediate responsibility.
Read provision for the helpless and institutions that remove the need to beg.
Keep the reported effort to meet immediate needs across religions and nationalities.
shortened: Before my departure for America the poor of all nationalities came to me, Persians and Turks, Arabs and Syrians, Greeks and Europeans etc. belonging to all religions and faiths.

However you see that although these difficulties exist I do not send away one man without satisfying in some way his immediate want. The worst condition of life is, when one is in urgent need of the means of livelihood. It is indeed very sad if a person begs assistance and one is unable to relieve him from the burden or contribute something toward his relief.

order.why: Read the reported uses of wealth for the vulnerable, science, and public welfare.
Consider the reported significance of educating children whose families cannot afford it.
Read the reported call for rulers to address avoidable poverty.
Keep the reported hope of heightened sensitivity to surrounding deprivation.
Consider the reported challenge to work made into drudgery.
Read livelihood through crafts and professions as commendable.
Place lawful earning above wealth wrongfully gathered.
Consider business and crafts as occasions to demonstrate trustworthiness.
Read the reported praise of rightly administered resources.
Keep use of material means together with trust in their Provider.
Read the rejection of begging in religion’s name beside the wealthy person’s duty to give.
shortened: No deed is more abhorrent than begging among people in the name of Truth.

However, the wealthy must be mindful of the poor, for the station of the patient among the poor is great in the sight of God. By My life! No station equals it save what God willeth. Blessed is the poor one who is patient and discrete, and blessed is the rich one who spends and prefers others.

order.why: Keep the parallel counsel to the generous rich and patient poor.
Consider those who have fallen from prosperity through age, weakness, or other causes.
shortened: Likewise with the wealthy and noble who through weakness and old age or other cause have fallen into poverty and abasement.

order.why: Rejects extremes of wealth and poverty and calls for laws and generosity that secure wellbeing.
Read love for the poor together with generosity, humility, and modest rule.
shortened: Verily, We love every patient poor one, every generous rich one, every humble elder, and every modest ruler. By My life! I love the poor and am with them and hear their cry.

order.why: Keep the source’s affirmation of bread withheld from no one.
shortened: Was it not evident to thee that this servant withholdeth not bread from anyone, nor hath He ever reproached any soul concerning bread, nor denied the riches of this world to any person?

order.why: Read voluntary sharing within the source’s specific discussion of compulsory dispositions.
shortened: The "sharing" and "equality", however, which are mentioned in the Divine Teachings denote measures that are undertaken voluntarily; in other words, should anyone of his own free will have mercy on the poor, and with the utmost gladness bestow upon them his wealth, such a person is favoured in the Court of Grandeur.

As for the new thoughts current in some European countries, these have to do with compulsory, not voluntary, dispositions, which are destructive of the body politic, and a cause of chaos and confusion in all lands.

order.why: Keep the warning against hoarding beside the prohibition on taking others’ property.
shortened: Those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the path of God, God will surely punish them for what they have hoarded - and who is more truthful in speech than God? This is the inner meaning, but outwardly the property of others is forbidden unto you. Beware lest ye deal treacherously with any soul or dispose of their property without their leave.

order.why: Consider spending from what has been bestowed.
shortened: Spend some of what God hath bestowed upon you through His grace - thereby will that which ye possess increase. The Mother Book with Him doth testify to this.

order.why: Read the reported rich giver through the happiness brought to humanity.
shortened: The patient poor are better than the thankful rich. But the thankful poor are better than the patient poor. And the best of all is the rich-giver who is free from temptations or tests, who becomes the cause of the happiness of mankind.

order.why: Keep the reported purpose of saving wealth tied to service to the poor.
shortened: Wealth is good for such times - otherwise what good is it? One should save and preserve it, and if successful in such an endeavor, one's heart is gladdened that, praise be to God, one has succeeded in rendering some service to the poor.

order.why: Read the reported example of great wealth without giving or comfort.
Retain the reported rebuke of stinginess within its narrative.
Consider a small accepted gift beside royal treasure.
shortened: In this glorious Dispensation the treasures laid up by kings and queens are not worthy of mention, nor will they be acceptable in the Presence of God. However, a grain of mustard offered by His loved ones will be extolled in the exalted court of His holiness and invested with the ornament of His acceptance.

order.why: Read courtesy as a measure of a person beyond possessions.
Keep the source’s refusal of worldly distinctions as spiritual measures.
shortened: Today neither loftiness nor lowliness, poverty nor wealth, lineage nor descent, weakness nor strength can be observed. Whosoever hath recognized the peerless Beloved - his is true wealth and spiritual station.

order.why: Read the absence of shame in lacking wealth and pride in possessing it.
shortened: Glorified be He Who hath adorned poverty with the ornament of pride through His words: "Poverty is My glory." Thus did the Tongue of Revelation speak aforetime, as every discerning soul doth testify.
Whatsoever is witnessed in the world of wealth, riches, treasures and the like belong to God. There is no shame in their absence, nor pride in their presence.

order.why: Consider the biblical camel image together with the rich person whose possessions do not hinder.
shortened: Today, however, most of those who sit at that table are the poor, and this is why Christ hath said blessed are the poor, for riches do prevent the rich from entering the Kingdom; and again, He saith, "It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the Kingdom of God."1 If, however, the wealth of this world, and worldly glory and repute, do not block his entry therein, that rich man will be favored at the Holy Threshold and accepted by the Lord of the Kingdom.

order.why: Read the parallel reported blessing of a detached wealthy person.
Consider examples of riches that did not prevent sacrifice and love.
shortened: How many souls whose wealth, glory and riches did not prevent them from the Lord of Names - they were set ablaze with the fire of divine love and bore in His path that which the eye of the world had never seen.

order.why: Keep the acknowledgment of differing responses among wealthy believers.
shortened: In this divine age some of the wealthy ones have, praise be to God, been successful, but some have been deprived.

order.why: Read wealth as capable of either obstruction or service.
Consider the reported distinction between material condition and detachment.
shortened: Material favors sometimes deprive us of spiritual favors and material rest of spiritual rest.
Riches did not prove an obstacle for them and they are like unto stars in the heaven of both worlds - flames of reality.
There are many rich people who are severed and many poor who are not.

order.why: Read the reported freedom to serve through changing circumstances.
Keep the rooted tree of assurance beside help offered to the weak.
shortened: In spite of poverty he acquires a sense of affluence and in a state of riches and power he offers help and protection to the weak because the well-assured soul is like a tree which has strong roots and is not shaken by any event.
How many are the people who have all means of comfort, luxury, security and wealth and every means of enjoyment and good living, yet they have no peace of mind and are ever anxious and uneasy!

order.why: Read gratitude and generosity in the source’s distinction between earthly and heavenly wealth.
shortened: And regarding the question of wealth and riches - what is meant is true wealth and heavenly riches, and this is an eternal bounty that will become complete and all-encompassing on the day when "God will enrich all through His abundance." This is specific to the loved ones of God. As for worldly wealth, all peoples share in it, meaning that in other communities too there exist those who are materially wealthy. Nevertheless, if someone wealthy is grateful and generous, they are certainly accepted and beloved, as mentioned in the divine Tablets: "When we find, we prefer others, and when we lose, we are grateful."

order.why: Consider the passing of prosperity and abasement.
Read the transience of possessions and the call to detachment.
shortened: Say: Rejoice not in the things ye possess; tonight they are yours, tomorrow others will possess them.
What advantage is there in the earthly things which men possess? That which shall profit them, they have utterly neglected.

Cast away that which ye possess, and, on the wings of detachment, soar beyond all created things. Thus biddeth you the Lord of creation, the movement of Whose Pen hath revolutionized the soul of mankind.

order.why: Keep the reported shifting sandhills as an image of unstable fortune.
Consider the question about the benefit of what ancestors amassed.
shortened: Do they imagine that what they possess will profit them? Nay, by the Lord of all worlds! Did what their fathers amassed benefit them?

order.why: Read the warning about attachment and the fate of property after death.
Consider ambitions that cannot accompany a person beyond death.
shortened: One craveth riches, another thirsteth for glory and still another yearneth for fame, for art, for prosperity and the like. Yet finally all are doomed to loss and disappointment. One and all they leave behind them all that is theirs and empty-handed hasten to the realm beyond, and all their labours shall be in vain.

order.why: Read the source’s warning that perishable things cannot secure independence.
Retain the reported quotation from the Will and Testament about peril in earthly riches.
shortened: I said to him, "The Shaykh-i-Kabir has left a Will and Testament in His own hand and seal, and defined in it the inheritance of His heir: 'Although the Realm of Glory hath none of the vanities of the world, yet within the treasury of trust and resignation We have bequeathed to Our heirs an excellent and priceless heritage. Earthly treasures We have not bequeathed, nor have We added such cares as they entail. By God! In earthly riches fear is hidden and peril is concealed.

order.why: Read the reported Bowery Mission address on anxiety and separation from possessions.
shortened: Even this earth's happiness does not depend upon wealth. You will find many of the wealthy exposed to dangers and troubled by difficulties, and in their last moments upon the bed of death there remains the regret that they must be separated from that to which their hearts are so attached.

order.why: Consider contentment as the foundation of comfort.
Keep the concise preference for ease and contentment.
Read happiness through freedom of spirit and human perfections.
Consider the reported contentment amid either wealth or poverty.
Keep the reported cultural comparison attributed to its conversation.
Read the reported bird image as a challenge to insatiable desire.
Keep the reported comparison of enjoyment at rich and poor tables in its own voice.
shortened: Kings never derive as much pleasure from their tables and delicious foods as the poor derive from plain bread. Why? Because due to their abundance of blessings, the bodies of kings do not have much desire, while the body of the poor person has the utmost desire.

order.why: Consider the reported concentration of ambition upon wealth.
shortened: The objective point of a soul is the acquirement of wealth. He concentrates all his ambition around the actualization of this cherished hope.

order.why: Read the source’s distinction between currency and true wealth through love.
shortened: Dirhams and dinars are not the measure of true wealth; its measure, rather, is the love of Him Who is the Beauteous, the Unconstrained.
How many are they who, though rich in dinars, are yet the poorest of God's creatures; for, even as is witnessed, each day their greed for gain increaseth, and their avarice waxeth more intense.

order.why: Keep the concise warning against being deluded by possessions.
shortened: The people have been deluded by their wealth and it hath prevented them from My Straight Path.

order.why: Consider wealth occupying attention away from the intended destination.
Read gold as an image of the test of attachment.
shortened: In the Hidden Words We said: "O Son of Being! Busy not thyself with this world, for with fire We test the gold, and with gold We test Our servants." On the day of reckoning they were occupied with riches and remained heedless and veiled from the wealthy and self-subsisting Lord.

order.why: Retain the reported warning about hardening of the heart.
shortened: "Unless the souls are believers in God and assured in the verses of God, wealth causes the hearts to be hardened and without light."

order.why: Read the reported relation of fortune to forgetting or turning toward God.
Keep the reported narrative of wealth, forgetfulness, loss, and repentance.
shortened: After he attained his goal and became wealthy, he forgot all.
Before long he lost all his wealth and repented on His threshold.
At the end, he died in poverty.

order.why: Read the particular warning of possessions becoming burdens.
shortened: Do not imagine that they will derive any benefit from these properties or gain any advantage. Rather, in the end these possessions will become a burden and this wealth a curse.

order.why: Consider the Bab’s account of the limits of wealth and children as supports.
Read the reported museum reflection on the use of resources and effort.
Keep the reported decision concerning Carnegie’s invitation in its historical setting.
shortened: Even in New York, the famous Carnegie, who is the wealthiest person there, repeatedly requested that I come to his home. I did not accept. The Consul General of Iran mediated several times. I said if he were a poor person, I would have gone to his home, but since he is the foremost among the wealthy and is famous, therefore it is not advisable.

order.why: Read the reported question about social scorn when rich and poor associate.
Consider the reported joy in gatherings of people in poverty.
Keep the reported Salvation Army address and its Christian reference.
shortened: This is what Christ states in the Gospels. 'It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle that for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God.' This testimony of Christ of the exaltation of the poor ones in the sight of God is sufficient.

order.why: Read the reported contrast of reliance on wealth and trust in God.
shortened: The poor are nearer the kingdom of heaven than the rich. The hope of the rich is in their wealth, but the trust of the poor is in God.

order.why: Retain the report’s forceful generalizations about accumulation as its attributed claims.
Keep the reported encounter with the impoverished man in Baghdad.
shortened: When I was in Bagdad, one day I was walking through the poor quarter of the city. I saw an old poor Arab standing in front of store. He had neither hat nor shoes and wore only a long tattered coat over his naked body. He had no shirt on himself. Between his coat and his skin he had a loaf of coarse black bread.

order.why: Read the reported contrast of circumstances and opportunities for generosity.
Consider poverty as absence within the reported philosophical explanation.
shortened: GOD did not create any evil thing. GOD did not create man poor. Poverty is only the lack of riches.

order.why: Keep the parallel account of absence with its examples.
Read the reported distinction between motives that develop the world and ultimate value.
Consider the recollection of having one garment and its counsel amid hardship.
Read acceptance of material relief during imprisonment without making it the court’s purpose.
shortened: We did not refuse such material benefits as could relieve Us from Our afflictions. Every one of Our companions, however, will bear Us witness that Our holy court is sanctified from, and far above, such material benefits. We have nevertheless accepted, while confined in this Prison, those things of which the infidels have striven to deprive Us.

order.why: Keep the particular reply about debt and outward hardship.
shortened: As for the matter of the sum you requested to pay your debt: First, although the Ancient Beauty, may my spirit be sacrificed for His dust, opened the doors of the treasuries of existence to the faces of His servants and immersed this helpless one in the sea of wealth, yet temporarily, outwardly, due to wisdom He ordained complete hardship - treasure in the sleeve but empty purse - so that all the friends would be known and recognized among the peoples of the world for their sanctity and detachment.

order.why: Read the account of economic distress in Iran as a historical letter.
shortened: Praise be to God, not one of the friends in this land has yet eaten barley bread; through divine bounty, blessing and favor they pass their days in utmost ease and contentment. The recession is throughout Iran. The One God is witness that what merchants and others have written in their letters would sadden every friend and grieve every loved one.

order.why: Consider the source’s account of changing circumstances among the Prophet’s companions.
Keep the particular depiction of hardship on the divine path.
shortened: Yet all lived in utmost hardship and difficulty, and most in extreme poverty and need.
From this blessed verse it is clear and evident that whoever travels the divine path, the wealthy become poor, not the poor wealthy - it works in reverse.

order.why: Read the bankruptcy letter’s personal counsel without generalizing it into a rejection of honest commerce.
shortened: Though you have newly beaten the drum of bankruptcy, we have long been sounding its trumpet and beating its drum. You have become harmonious with us and entered upon the path of the righteous ones.

However, the condition is this: that you do not sully yourself again and do not immerse yourself once more in the sea of commerce whose end is disgrace and loss. Rather, seek detachment and pursue severance, and think of the greatest profit and most glorious gain and trade in the market of His Holiness the King of Oneness.

order.why: Keep the challenging personal counsel about gratitude amid want.
shortened: What a pity that someone like you should become so distraught and distressed from want. We had hoped that someone like you, if afflicted with grinding poverty, would increase in joy and thanksgiving and give others the thread of patience and gratitude.

order.why: Read the teacher’s outward poverty beside spiritual purpose.
Retain the reported equanimity toward extreme circumstances.
shortened: I wish for the happiness and prosperity of the believers even in this material world, but they must not be attracted by it or attached to it. Extreme wealth or utter poverty should be equal to them.

order.why: Consider the source’s relation between poverty and detachment.
Distinguish the faqir’s spiritual poverty from lack of worldly goods.
Keep the brief exaltation of poverty within that spiritual register.
Read love as the essence of wealth.
Consider generosity and excellence of soul as the measure of prosperity.
shortened: O servant of Baha! Wealth and prosperity do not consist in worldly goods but rather in generosity and excellence of soul. In other words, he who finds the true layers of gold and discovers the Supreme Treasure of the Blessed Beauty in the divine mines is indeed the one who will be rich in both worlds and prosperous in the highest heaven.

order.why: Read possessions that thieves cannot take beside those they can.
Consider sovereignty as a treasury of the soul.
Read the empty purse and treasure in the sleeve as spiritual giving.
shortened: My intention was that although the blessed purse is empty, there should be a treasure in the sleeve - that you should distribute heavenly wealth so that hearts become enriched with divine riches.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of enduring riches.
Consider earthly difficulty beside comfort in the divine realm.
Read the treasure described as increasing and inexhaustible.
shortened: Praise be to God that you have found your way to the treasures of the Kingdom, and this treasure will never end as it is an everlasting wealth. There is no loss or damage in it; day by day it increases.

order.why: Keep the paradox of empty pockets and inward wealth.
Read the source’s detached souls and heavenly treasures with its preserved omission.
Consider the reversal of earthly rank through spiritual treasure.
Read the source’s distinction of material and true wealth.
Keep the reported prayerful hope for an enriched heart.
shortened: True wealth is the wealth of the Kingdom of God. The heart of man must be rich. Often it has happened that a person is poor but is wealthy; on the other hand a soul may possess one hundred million but he is poor. Every treasury, in this world, is subject to exhaustion, save the treasury of the Kingdom which is inexhaustible. I hope that thou mayst become rich through the treasury of the Kingdom.
His Holiness Christ and all the prophets were poor.

order.why: Read the reported recollection of being created rich.
Keep the reported assurance to those poor in outward means.
Read the reported ocean of true wealth as encouragement.
Consider recognition as spiritual wealth in the source’s own terms.
Keep the related description of recognition and riches.
shortened: They who are today turned toward the Most Exalted Horizon and have attained the recognition of the Lord of Names are accounted before God as the most wealthy among His servants.

order.why: Read faith as the highest wealth within the source’s account.
Consider possession and deprivation measured against the divine gift.
Read the source’s affirmation of divine giving and withholding.
shortened: Know thou with certain knowledge that wealth, riches, exaltation and sublimity have ever been and shall ever be in the grasp of God's power. He giveth and He withholdeth, and He is the Powerful, the Mighty.

order.why: Close the linked readings with a prayer for provision, mercy, and blessing.
Retain the supplied statement on diverse livelihoods and its unresolved opening omission.
Read the supplied invitation to attend to what God has sent down.
Close with the supplied Proverbs prayer for sufficiency, retaining its original wording and citation.

questions: What changes when wealth and poverty are evaluated through their effects on character and conduct?
How can honest earning, lawful enjoyment, generosity, and detachment support one another in practice?
What responsibilities arise when people in poverty are described as a trust, and how might communities fulfill them?
How does the prayer in Proverbs illuminate the different temptations associated with abundance and deprivation?
What distinctions are needed when reading spiritual poverty alongside passages calling for material relief?
Which forms of wealth could be cultivated and shared without diminishing, and how might they guide the use of material resources?

references.label: 1 · Proverbs 30:7–9 · Sufficiency and integrity
references.note: Read the King James Version of the prayer for freedom from falsehood and for sufficient food, with its concern about both abundance and deprivation. Compare this with the compilation’s evaluation of wealth through its effects. The supplied quotation remains as imported; this linked primary text provides a separate reading of the passage.

subjects.displayTitle: Iran: memory, suffering, and the work of renewal
subjects.introduction: Love for a homeland is rarely simple, and for Iran it holds pride, grief, reproach and hope in a single breath. Bahá’u’lláh addresses the people of Iran as the dawning-places of mercy whose learning once lit the regions of the world, and then asks how they came to turn upon themselves and their friends. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá remembers a Persia that was the heart of the world, the source of sciences and arts, and refuses to believe its people inherently deficient; he calls them to wake from a long sleep, to acquire knowledge, build railways, educate daughters and sons, and serve the welfare of all. His prayer for Persia asks, after loss, for a new springtime in which barren dust turns into a rose garden. To love a country in this way leads naturally to the relationship between government and people, to the long argument over constitutional rule and parliaments, and to the meeting of East and West. The Analects’ image of virtuous rule as a polar star, and its distinction between merely avoiding punishment and cultivating character, offers a companion thought on what renewal finally asks of those who govern [1].
subjects.arc: Begin with compassion and a vision of service, examine education and renewal, revisit cultural memory, then read conflict and criticism in historical context before returning to hope and prayer.

order.why: Open with the appeal from remembered compassion and learning to concern over mutual destruction.
shortened: The Great Announcement proclaimeth: O people of Iran! Ye have been the dawning-places of mercy and the daysprings of compassion and love. The regions of the world were illumined and adorned with the light of your knowledge. How is it that ye have arisen to destroy yourselves and your friends?

order.why: Read the reported hope for sciences, arts, moral service, and universal peace.
shortened: May Iranians advance to such a degree that they will shine throughout all regions, become the example for all nations, establish the virtues of the human world, and progress both materially and culturally. May Iran become the center of sciences and arts and the source of crafts and innovations. May it serve the world of morality, become the cause of promoting universal peace. May it establish unprecedented laws and ordinances that will serve as a model throughout all regions, and this is not difficult for God to accomplish.

order.why: Make acquiring knowledge and exerting effort for people’s advancement central.
Consider the concrete railway proposal and its expected regional benefits.
Read the reported aims of commerce, education, and scientific attainment.
Keep the reported measure of national distinction in the unity of humanity.
shortened: Because the Sun of Reality has risen from the horizon of Iran, the Iranians must act in such a way that the realm of Iran becomes the crown of the world - and that is the unity of the human world and the union and agreement of all humanity.
The Iranians should attain to this bounty and triumph more than others.

order.why: Read the reported hope that other lands benefit from what arose in Iran.
Consider newcomers as possible contributors to progress and worldwide illumination.
shortened: Through the great bounty of the Merciful Lord, I hope that each of these newcomers will become the cause of Iran's progress and the nobility of Iranians. Indeed, may they shine like lamps in the assembly of the world and gleam like bright stars from the horizon of the world.
Iran will become the center of divine inspirations and the source of endless bounties for humanity.

order.why: Read the call to take a lead in knowledge.
shortened: Now is the time for you to take the lead and bring the melody of the angel of the Supreme Concourse to the ears of humanity, so that perhaps the Persian people in this divine cycle may be so stirred to enthusiasm and excitement that they may snatch the ball of precedence and leadership from all others in the arena of knowledge.

order.why: Keep the need for noble souls and new foundations beside the critique of accumulation.
shortened: Iran is desolate and in need of noble souls who would establish new foundations for Iran's prosperity. But alas, alas! Previously all were drowning in desires, having no aim except amassing worldly ornaments.

order.why: Read the promised relation of action to material and spiritual progress.
shortened: If this is carried out, rest assured that in a short time Iran will become bright and illumined like the full moon and will make extraordinary progress in all material and spiritual degrees.

order.why: Consider the call to effort in the homeland of the Faith’s central Figures.
shortened: Strive then and exert a mighty effort, for Persia is the homeland of the compassionate Beloved, and Fars the dawning-place of the resplendent Morn. Perchance, through the high endeavours of the friends, the inhabitants of that land may perceive the rays of that luminous Orb, and may receive their portion of manifold grace from the Lord of tokens and signs.

order.why: Read the Secret of Divine Civilization’s 1875 address and its historical rhetoric of memory and reform.
shortened: O people of Persia! Look into those blossoming pages that tell of another day, a time long past. Read them and wonder; see the great sight. Iran in that day was as the heart of the world; she was the bright torch flaming in the assemblage of mankind. Her power and glory shone out like the morning above the world's horizons, and the splendor of her learning cast its rays over East and West.

O people of Persia! Awake from your drunken sleep! Rise up from your lethargy! Be fair in your judgment: will the dictates of honor permit this holy land, once the wellspring of world civilization, the source of glory and joy for all mankind, the envy of East and West, to remain an object of pity, deplored by all nations?

order.why: Consider legendary kings transformed into images of guidance and love.
Keep the reported Naw-Ruz narrative and chronology attributed to its source.
Read the related reported account of the festival and its shared celebration.
Retain the source’s account of Iran between Alexander and Ardashir as its historical interpretation.
Keep the reported linguistic history and chronology in its own voice.
Read the reported account of Barbad and Farabi without making it an editorial history of music.
Consider the address to Parsis through decline and renewed spiritual spring.
shortened: The realm of Iran is the Eastern clime and has been the country of the godly ones from the beginning. For a time, there came a decline and negligence appeared. The moon of its glory's zenith set, and the star of its wisdom and knowledge descended.

Time passed, and now again the time of good fortune has arrived and the sun of auspicious destiny has dawned. The breeze of divine favor has blown upon this clime and the light of bounty has shone forth. The brilliant sun has risen from the Eastern realm and the life-giving fragrance has wafted from the land of Iran.

order.why: Read the invitation to Zoroastrians to celebrate spiritual renewal.
Keep the reported landscape and future hope in its personal address.
shortened: Now from this you can judge what will be the future of Persia which is the birthplace of the Blessed Perfection, Baha'u'llah. Its climate is delightful, its soil is rich, its waters salubrious, its gardens charming, its meadows green and its topography varied.

order.why: Consider the Pishdadian allusion as an image of a dawning day.
shortened: I hope that He will make Iran once again the envy of the world and exalt the Persians in both worlds, that faces may become radiant and hearts may become the repository of the mysteries of the Lord of Bounties.
Glad tidings unto you that the night of deprivation hath come to an end and the bright day of the Pishdadians hath dawned anew.

order.why: Read the reported contrast of past glory and present distress leading to science and industry.
shortened: There was a time when Persia was like a fragrant Bouquet perfuming all the nostrils and she was the center of the glory and honor of the world of humanity. The inhabitants of Persia from a social, industrial, political and moral standpoint were superior to the rest of mankind.
Now the conditions are changed and the same lofty standard is not kept waving aloft. Like a great giant she is prostrated on the ground while groaning with a pitiful voice.

As Persia has experienced these sad events, the Lord in his Mercy has willed it to illumine that country and it is assured that her future condition will be more glorious than the past and that she may advance greatly along the path of science, industry and arts.

order.why: Consider the source’s account of revelation arising amid many accomplished nations.
shortened: O beloved of the Lord! There exist upon this terrestrial globe mighty peoples, tribes, nations, and governments, each of which is renowned in the East and the West for its attainments, arts and sciences. Yet, by virtue of the divine favours, it is above the horizon of Iran that the Daystar of Truth hath risen and hath cast its merciful rays over every land.

order.why: Keep the particular claim of Iran’s distinction through spiritual bounty.
shortened: Surely Iran has superiority over other regions because it was specially endowed with this bounty. But other regions received illumination from the land of Iran and acquired lights from those regions.

order.why: Read the distinction between political independence and enduring spiritual illumination.
Consider promised development alongside the warning that others may receive the Faith first.
shortened: Baha'u'llah, however, has illumined that land, and will surely raise her high in the eyes of all the world. That country shall so advance and develop as to excite the envy and admiration of the East and the West.
But alas! This Cause, though it first appeared in Persia, yet eventually it shall be seen how the peoples of Europe have wrested it from its hands! Take note of this and remember it in future.

order.why: Keep the theological account of progress in the chapter on Baha’u’llah.
shortened: As to Persia, which to this day remains in such an abject and ruinous state, every man of wisdom, whether from within or without her borders, who knows her true state of affairs recognizes that her progress, her prosperity, and her civilization depend entirely upon the promulgation of the teachings and the dissemination of the principles of this glorious Being.

order.why: Read the critique of imitation alongside the source’s account of spiritual, moral, and material renewal.
shortened: They imagine that through imitating the people of the West and through the confused thoughts of the people of Iran, Persia will progress. Alas! Alas! Despite God having caused such a brilliant Sun to rise from the horizon of Iran, whose rays have struck both East and West, and having established such a Covenant that is the cause of Iran's eternal glory and the means of progress in all aspects - whether material, moral, or political - this Most Great Force which gives life to Iran, the Iranians are heedless of it and wish to revive Iran through these vain thoughts.

order.why: Keep the source’s remedy and its warning about unexamined following.
shortened: Today the success and prosperity of Iran and Iranians lies in this. And now too it is submitted that this is the brilliant star, this is the life-giving remedy. If you desire Iran's ascent to Saturn's height, you must serve at the divine court so the All-Merciful's palace gate may open. Otherwise the future will be like the past and Iranians will remain followers and imitators of mufti and judge.

order.why: Read the reported assessment of education and Mirza Taqi Khan in its historical setting.
shortened: Mirza Taqi Khan, the Prime Minister, although he committed such oppression against the Cause that no one had ever done before, nevertheless laid foundations in political affairs and national matters that truly possessed the utmost firmness, even though he had never entered any school in Europe.
Yes, proper education assists one who is wise, aware and confirmed, but if there is no innate knowledge and divine confirmation, what fruit and effect does mere education have?

order.why: Consider the letter’s demand for education with its preserved omissions.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! News of thine arrival in Kirman reached us and thy letter was perused...
...all of Iran is in need of education. Until now no significant enlightened souls have appeared in the assemblies of Iran, and if there be any, "the rare is as the non-existent."

order.why: Read the reported awakening of women as a sign of wider change.
shortened: This great woman's movement which is stirring and vibrating all round the whole world is a sign of spirit awakening; even in Persia they stir, they awake, and many have become Bahaists and are freed from the old chains.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of readiness to hear extending across East and West.
shortened: Today Iran, nay rather the East and the West, has attained a wondrous readiness to hear the call of the Most Merciful Lord. Ears have opened and souls are seeking to hear the mystery.

order.why: Consider the contrast of awakened strangers and inattentive familiars.
shortened: It is hoped that the Iranians too will awaken, move beyond metaphor, become aware of and comprehend the truth, and realize that the Sun of Truth has risen from the dawning-place of Iran and has shed its rays upon all horizons. Strange it is that strangers have awakened while familiars remain asleep in the bed of heedlessness.

order.why: Read the concise comparison with Americans as the source’s assessment.
shortened: The Iranians are still asleep while the Americans have awakened.

order.why: Keep the address urging recognition of a spiritual opportunity.
shortened: Say unto them: O Persians! The East and West of the world are astir, and the holy fragrances have perfumed the nostrils of the most distant lands. How is it that ye, being Persians, remain deprived and bereft? Such a crown hath God placed upon your heads, and such a brilliant star hath risen from your horizon - how is it that ye still wander in darkness? This is strange and peculiar.

order.why: Read the reported owner-and-house image within its forceful admonition.
shortened: Alas! still the majority of the inhabitants of Persia are in sound sleep and have not heard, neither are they informed with the Most Eminent Bestowal.

The owner of the house has come at the door but the dwellers in the house have shut the door and do not desire to let him in. They have treated the friend as though he was a stranger and the known as though he was unknown. They seem to say: "We are satisfied with this degradation. We are comfortable amidst all these distractions, dissipations, groveling dirt and uncleanliness. We do not want the owner of the house. We are not seeking his Faith.

order.why: Retain the related reported statement about inattention and its omission.
shortened: The inhabitants of Persia are yet sleep, although God has demonstrated to them his Cause in so many ways... If this Cause had appeared in Europe and America, by this time all those regions would have become illumined and the souls would have become awakened.

order.why: Consider the reported lament over failure to recognize a gift.
Keep the reported claim about Persia’s lost opportunity in its own voice.
shortened: He spoke of the spread of civilization from the East to the West, saying: "What a blessing God bestowed upon the Persians but they could not appreciate it! Had they not been ungrateful, the government of Persia would have ranked first in the world.

order.why: Read the reported counterfactual about accepting divine teachings.
Keep the related reported reference to necessary laws and principles.
Read the reported counsel given to Persian dignitaries during the European journey.
shortened: We have counseled the statesmen of Persia to the utmost of our ability, but no one listened or accepted our advice. While travelling in Europe, I met many of the Persian Princes, Ministers and prominent men of that ancient country, and told them the truth of the matter; but the majority of them did not like it.

order.why: Retain the concise reported recollection of advice unheard.
Consider the reported purpose of the Paris stay for Persian listeners.
Read the reported turn toward the West and its hope for the East.
Keep the reported expectation of esteem for Persia through the Faith.
Read the letter’s hope that exiles might render service despite political conflict.
Place the dated account of continuing changes within its particular moment.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! Thy letter dated the 7th of Dhi'l-Hajjih 1339 was received. The world of humanity, particularly Iran, is in great turmoil, and changes and transformations in all conditions follow one after another.

order.why: Hear the receipt of a letter of grief about Persia’s condition.
Consider the distress of a friend and reformer.
Read the source’s account of civil conflict and lost tranquility.
Keep the description of Fars and Iran as afflicted.
Read Iran’s turmoil alongside the source’s wider view of a troubled world.
Consider the letter’s description of chaos and self-absorption.
shortened: Currently in Iran there is such chaos that it defies description. Everyone is occupied with themselves and has no opportunity to deal with others.

order.why: Keep the message about difficulties among government and people.
Read the longing for refuge amid strife and bloodshed.
shortened: The peoples of Persia are busied with their own selves, and beneath the weight of strife and bloodshed, the majority are weary of life and existence. They seek a refuge; yet there is no place to flee to, no refuge that any one can seek, no haven to repair unto, and no shelter to find, except the Kingdom of Abha that hath caused the whole world to be stirred and shaken, and will, ere long bring about the prosperity of Persia and will cause her peoples to become endeared to them of this world and of the next.

order.why: Consider the distinction between overthrowing tyranny and establishing freedom.
Read the source’s account of upheaval and homelessness.
Keep travel counsel for women and men tied to the reported insecurity of that time.
Read the letter’s account of security, oppression, and historical generalizations as its own testimony.
shortened: In these days, due to the counsels of Abdu'l-Baha, in all the cities of Iran the friends are reposing in the cradle of peace and security, while during this upheaval all other parties have been in the utmost distress. However, in the regions of Khurasan until now the friends remain caught in the grip of oppression and enmity.

O what regret upon them! In human virtues other regions, even warlike Africans, have progressed, while Iran - which in ancient times was the center of humanity and civilization and was renowned throughout the horizons for its nobility - is now caught in such conditions: no modesty or shame, no justice or faithfulness, no fear of God.

order.why: Keep the Tablet on martyrs within its lament over persecution and its rhetorical comparisons.
shortened: In this luminous age, which is the mighty century of the Lord, when from the rays of the Sun of Truth the lights of civilization have spread to all regions, and human perfections and divine virtues are diffused like the dawning light in East and West to such a degree that savagery and bloodthirstiness among humankind have become abandoned customs--nay, in civilized countries entirely forgotten--and when religious persecutions have wholly ceased and ignorant prejudices been nullified, and among peoples and tribes, aside from international wars and political thoughts, no conflict, contention or strife remains, and all nations and peoples rest in the cradle of peace and security, and all communities are safe from the evil of oppressors and protected in an impregnable fortress--yet in Iran, when the divine call was raised and the luminous dawn broke and the Sun of Truth shone forth, souls who had been rescued from the lowest depths of ignorance attained the highest degrees of humanity and became the center of divine inspirations.

order.why: Read the detailed rebuke of plunder, hypocrisy, and failures of justice.
shortened: Justice and truthfulness have become so absent and concealed that no trace thereof can be found amongst the people. The horizons of the heaven of truth have been darkened by the gloom of the people of hypocrisy. Most of the decrees of the administrative circles of Iran have been and continue to be contrary to that which justice and fairness command. They have no purpose save vain ornaments. Day and night they are occupied with plunder and pillage.

order.why: Retain the source’s severe sectarian polemic as a historically situated denunciation.
Read the recalled Tablet of the World appeal against mutual destruction.
Keep the reported judgment about Qa’im-Maqam as a historical counterfactual.
Read the source’s account of Siyyid Fattah and Russian intervention without adding historical claims.
Retain the reported recollection concerning the Mushir with its attribution.
Read the source’s distinction between royal intention and obstructive religious leaders.
Consider the letter’s grief and its allocation of responsibility for conflict.
Keep the critique of edicts issued without political understanding.
Read the concise criticism of ignorant leadership.
shortened: Consider what they have brought upon Iran. A people with such ignorant leaders and public affairs in their hands will not fare better than this.

order.why: Retain the account of the National Assembly and followers of Yahya as the source’s assessment.
Consider the distinction between parliamentary clamor and investigation of public welfare.
Read the letter’s critique of parties across political periods.
Keep the stated chronology and assessment of independence in their original setting.
Read the reported criticism of party conflict in 1913.
shortened: I said these current details are causes of ruin - these differences, these various parties, one democratic and one moderate, day by day they are destroying Iran. Compare Iran's current condition with ten years ago. These differences have ruined Iran and are increasing day by day.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast of public good and personal profit.
Read the assessment of parties’ promises and consequences.
Keep the letter’s account of Iranian and worldwide upheaval and its figures attributed.
shortened: Observe how in the revolution of Iran, nay rather the turmoil of the entire world, what scenes appeared on this stage and finally all were rolled up with neither fruit nor trace, neither result nor news except ruin and dispersion and regret. Neither victor nor vanquished - both were in loss, for the blood of thirty million souls was spilled in vain and humanity was endangered and cities and villages were overturned without result or fruit.

order.why: Read the warning of foreign intervention through internal conflict.
shortened: This conflict will lead to foreign powers' intervention in Iran. At that time both sides will regret it, but regret and remorse will then benefit neither the people nor the government.

order.why: Consider the reported house image and relation between government and people.
shortened: The Persians destroyed their home with their own hands in the hope of building another one; but now they are left in the desert without a home or shelter.
We wrote and exhorted them, pointing out that the union of government and the people is like combining milk and honey; otherwise, the neighboring governments will encroach upon the country.

order.why: Keep the reported milk-and-honey counsel and its warning of intervention.
shortened: At the outset of that revolution in Persia known as the Constitutional Revolution, I wrote again and again that until such time as that government and its people become commingled, even as milk and honey, their success and prosperity will remain entirely unattainable. Persia shall fall into ruin, and the governments of its neighbouring realms will ultimately meddle in its affairs...

order.why: Read the possibility of repair through love, unity, and recognition of well-wishers.
shortened: Now that the calamity of following the fatwas of thoughtless clerics has become apparent, and the result of party divisions has become evident, if they now awaken and undertake to make amends for what was lost, they will no longer count the friends of God as strangers, and will not consider souls following their own desires as well-wishers and kind ones, will not count wolves as shepherds, and will engage in love and unity, uproot the foundation of division, and make the counsels and advice found in the sacred tablets their course of action, once again times will become sweet as sugar.

order.why: Consider the particular letter about depression, inflation, and factional conflict.
Keep the reported judgment about temporary reforms in its 1920 setting.
shortened: He stated: "Affairs have fallen into the hands of children, affairs have fallen into the hands of the base and incompetent. No authority remains for the sovereign. It will take long before Iran becomes Iran. Until it comes under the divine breaths of God, it is impossible. Whatever reforms are made are temporary."

order.why: Read the reported connection between public service and administration.
shortened: ...the discussion became general about the conditions of Persia and Turkey; the unfortunate reverses that these two Islamic nations have had during the last two generations, owing to the lack of public spirited servants and misadministration of the government affairs.
