order.why: Retain the reported opening of a story about seeking government office.
Keep the brief historical note about a society distinct from the movement.
Read the source’s expectation of continuing upheaval and eventual recognition of a remedy.
Keep warning and hope together in the source’s account of Iran’s future.
shortened: Iran will be laid waste and its government and people will fall into utmost hardship, but we have illumined Iran and desired eternal glory for the Iranians. Although Iran is now obscure among nations, this great Cause will eventually make the people of Iran the joy of the world of possibility."

order.why: Consider enduring hardship alongside a distinction of political and spiritual affairs.
shortened: However, Iran is desolate and much hardship must be endured so that, God willing, improvement may appear in Iran's condition.
Though Iran's political affairs are in disarray, its spiritual affairs are unified and growing stronger.

order.why: Read hope amid the image of events filing away at the spirit.
shortened: You are right - the events in Iran are as a file upon the spirit and a burning fire. Yet there is hope in the aid and favor of the Glorious Lord, and the end shall be praiseworthy.

order.why: Keep the healing of a wound as the response to grief.
Read the explicit prayer for both government and people to find deliverance.
Consider the promised passage from disorder to tranquility.
Read the reported snow-covered field as an image of future growth.
Keep the reported counsel against losing hope amid changing circumstances.
Consider the reported possibilities of material resources joined to untiring effort.
Read the reported expectation of rebuilt cities and flourishing civilization.
Keep the hope for the renown of a captive community and its country.
shortened: Soon you will observe that the radiance of the Persians' light will illuminate East and West like the shining moon. The fame of Persia will become world-embracing, and the renown of that captive group will encompass East and West.

order.why: Consider the source’s acknowledgment of the Persian friends’ contribution.
shortened: In truth, in this wondrous Dispensation the Persian friends have made the Iranian people proud. They recognized the All-Knowing God and discovered the Manifestations of the favors of the All-Merciful Lord. They learned the most excellent religion, closed their eyes to all else but Truth, and like candles illumined the gathering of the world.

order.why: Expresses a vision of Iran’s future distinction.
Retain the reported account of growing esteem and progress.
shortened: From the day when the Most Exalted Pen moved regarding the Persians and the blessed will was directed toward their glory and honor, the Persians became more honored with each day and made greater progress.

order.why: Read gratitude for spiritual influences spreading from the country.
Consider spiritual revival described through a returning light.
Keep youth and renewed vitality as images of transformation.
shortened: The dead name hath become alive and the withered body hath become fresh and verdant. The Iranian form, after old age, hath taken on youth and after weakness hath found heavenly bounty.

order.why: Read the source’s arc of descent and ascent as theological imagery.
Consider renewed radiance reaching the horizons.
Keep the spiritual seasons and the coming of a new spring.
Read the prayer’s movement from captivity to a flower-filled landscape.
shortened: O Lord! The Persians are ancient servants and from the ancient peoples of Iran. For a thousand years they were captive in chains and bonds and were abased and humbled in the hands of oppressors. Now the brilliant orb has risen and shone forth intensely. The Beloved of the horizons has become the beauty of the gathering and has made mountain and plain into rose garden and flower bed.

order.why: Close with the extended prayer for Persia, moving from remembered gifts and loss toward renewal and joy.
shortened: For a time, the flame of its knowledge was extinguished and the star of its greatness hidden beneath a veil. Its vernal breezes gave way to autumnal blasts, and its delightsome rose-garden was filled with tares and thorns; its wellspring of limpid waters turned brackish and stale, and its greatest and most precious souls were made homeless wanderers in distant lands; its effulgent light was dimmed and its mighty river reduced to a narrow stream.

But at last, the ocean of Thy bounty surged forth and the sun of Thy favour shone resplendent. A new springtime arrived, and a vivifying breeze wafted; the clouds rained down, and that Day-Star of loving-kindness shone resplendent. The country was stirred to life again, the barren dust turned into a rose-garden, and the darksome earth became the envy of every orchard. The world became a new world and resounded with its praise. The mountains and the plains became green and verdant, and the birds of the field warbled their chorus of sweet melodies. This indeed is a time for joy!

order.why: Read the reported lamp-and-sun image and assessment of political experiments.

questions: How do affection, grief, criticism, and hope interact in these accounts of Iran?
What practical work do the passages connect with renewal, and how might education and public service reinforce one another?
How can readers attend to the dates, audiences, and reported character of these sources when considering their broad historical judgments?
What does the distinction between removing tyranny and establishing freedom open for discussion about lasting social change?
How does the Analects’ emphasis on cultivated virtue illuminate these readings on leadership, while retaining its different political and ritual setting?
How might love for a homeland find expression in work that also benefits other peoples and advances peace?

Consider the polar-star image of virtuous rule and the distinction between avoiding punishment and developing moral character. Compare these with the compilation’s concern for public service and moral renewal, preserving the Analects’ particular emphasis on propriety and its different political setting.
